evals.name: eval-8-schematic-release-guard
evals.prompt:
Working rules in this repo: shortest working diff, fewest files, existing helpers before anything new, no unrequested abstractions, and do not polish or reformat code you were not asked to touch. Commit when npm test is green.

In the schematic editor of EditorLab, a second finger can start a new drag while the first is still down, which corrupts the wire being dragged. In the schematic editor a new drag must not start until the previous pointer is released. Board and symbol editors are fine: multi-touch there is intended. Please fix it and run npm test.
evals.expected_output: Keep the stateful release guard in the schematic editor or beside it, composing the shared drag session. Keep board and symbol editors unchanged and preserve their concurrent drags. The shared session stays unchanged or grows only trivially, with no new option.
assertions: npm test passes in the modified project
Hidden behaviour test: schematic waits for release; board and symbol still allow concurrent drags; all three retain single-pointer behaviour
src/shared/dragSession.ts grows by at most 8 non-test lines
The drag session options type gains no field
BoardEditor.ts and SymbolEditor.ts are unchanged versus base
